messages:
Jenna (Support): FYI customer on Dedicated Private reported 502s from their app to our hosted control plane. They say nothing changed on their side since yesterday. Can someone help triage?

Ravi (Eng Oncall): Can you paste the failing curl or client error and any TLS logs? 502 from our edge could be a TLS handshake abort if OCSP/CRL checks time out behind a restrictive egress policy.

Jenna (Support): Paste from the customer's app log: 

```
curl -v https://control.redwood-inference.example/v1/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://control.redwood-inference.example/v1/health/
*   Trying 10.1.2.45...
* Connected to control.redwood-inference.example (10.1.2.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* SSL certificate problem: certificate status unknown
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate status unknown
```

They also captured the systemd journal showing "TLS: certificate status unknown (OCSP)" and a short tcpdump showing the client never completed OCSP TCP handshake.

Marco (Eng-Infra): Do they have an outbound allowlist? OCSP/CRL responders are often on different domains/IPs and sometimes on port 80. If their firewall only allows our control plane IPs it will still fail cert validation. Ask the customer to run a dig +trace against the OCSP domain and a curl to the OCSP responder from the same host where the app runs.

Jenna (Support): Customer says they use an egress gateway with a tight allowlist. They ran `dig +short ocsp.comodoca.com` and got NXDOMAIN from their internal resolver. They also ran `curl -v http://ocsp.comodoca.com` and it times out from their app host.

Ravi (Eng Oncall): Bingo. Repro steps I'd ask them to run (share with customer):

1) From the app host: `dig +trace ocsp.comodoca.com` and `dig @8.8.8.8 ocsp.comodoca.com` to see if split-horizon is returning different answers.
2) `curl -v http://<ocsp-host>` (OCSP is often plain HTTP) and `curl -I https://control.redwood-inference.example` to see certificate stapling/OCSP stapled status.
3) `tcpdump -n -i any port 80 or port 443 or port 8080` while reproducing to capture blocked TCP resets/timeouts.

sre-bot: [alert] site-204 egress-block detected: outbound connections to known-ocsp-responder list failed from host app-12 (threshold triggered).

Marco (Eng-Infra): Quick checklist: allowlist outbound TCP/80 and TCP/443 to lista of OCSP/CRL domains (Comodo, DigiCert, Let's Encrypt, GlobalSign etc.), allow DNS resolution to public resolvers or ensure internal resolver forwards, and allow making short-lived outbound connections to those CDNs. If they're unwilling to change policy, a temporary workaround is to configure their TLS stack to accept stapled OCSP from our edge (if present) or to pin certs, but both have security trade-offs. Recommend allowlist.

Jenna (Support): Customer tried pointing to 8.8.8.8 and then `curl http://ocsp.comodoca.com` returned a valid response. After adding the ocsp domains to their egress allowlist and permitting outbound TCP/80, their app calls to `/v1/generate` started returning 200 again.

Ravi (Eng Oncall): Great. Can you ask them to confirm that the fix is persistent (reboot the gateway or fail over) and get us a confirmation that the issue is resolved? We'll draft a KB with the OCSP/CRL allowlist hints and recommended DNS config for Private/VPC customers.

Jenna (Support): Customer confirmed persistence after gateway restart. Marking as resolved from our side. I'll follow up with KB and include the diagnostics commands and the short list of domains/IP ranges they needed to add. :white_check_mark:

Marco (Eng-Infra): Also adding a note for product: consider documenting common OCSP responders and CRL URIs for our cert chain in the Private deployment guide so customers can pre-seed allowlists.

Ravi (Eng Oncall): Good call. Closing thread when KB is published. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
